response_text: Multiple *.c files are compiled into a single executable through a three-stage process. First the code is pre-processed. Here comments are removed from the code and any include files are found and copied in place of the #include tag that marked them. Additionally, macros which are not active are deleted from the code in this step. Next the code is compiled and turned into a .o file which is an object file. The last step is linking, where all functions calls are linked with their definitions, which means the computer searches where each of the functions are defined and pastes in their function definitions in the code at which point the file becomes an executable file. The linker essentially takes all the object files and combines them into one executable file that can be run by the computer.\n
